faqs.a: Ohm's Law: V = I x R. Voltage (volts) equals current (amps) times resistance (ohms). It describes how electricity flows through a resistor.
Joule's Law for electric power: P = V x I. Power (watts) equals voltage times current. Combined with Ohm's Law, you can also write P = I^2 x R or P = V^2 / R.
Measure the current and voltage. R = V / I. For example, 9 V across a circuit drawing 0.5 A means R = 9 / 0.5 = 18 ohms.
faqs.q: How do I find an unknown resistance?

faqs.a: Divide the voltage by the resistance: I = V / R. So 12 V across 4 ohms gives 3 amps. The resistor then dissipates P = 12 x 3 = 36 W.
faqs.q: How do I find the current?

faqs.a: P = V x I. A 12 V device drawing 2 A uses 24 W. For heating elements and bulbs, higher watts mean more heat or light.
faqs.q: How do I calculate power consumption?

faqs.a: Pick any pair you know: V and I, V and R, I and R, P and V, P and I, or P and R. The calculator solves the other two values plus power automatically.
faqs.q: Which two values do I need to enter?

ohms-law-calculator.formula:
Ohm's Law: V = I x R

Power: P = V x I = I^2 x R = V^2 / R

Rearranged:
I = V / R        R = V / I
V = sqrt(P x R)  I = sqrt(P / R)
P = V^2 / R      R = V^2 / P

Example: V = 12, R = 4 -> I = 12 / 4 = 3 A, P = 12 x 3 = 36 W.
howTo: Pick which pair of values you know: voltage and current, voltage and resistance, and so on.
All four values - voltage, current, resistance, and power - appear instantly.
Use the power result to check component ratings before building a circuit.
keyFacts: Ohm's Law: V = I x R. Published by Georg Ohm in 1827.
Power: P = V x I. Also P = I^2 x R and P = V^2 / R.
Doubling voltage across a fixed resistor quadruples the power (P = V^2 / R).
Resistors convert electric power into heat. That is why high-power resistors get hot.
Ohm's Law applies to resistive DC circuits. Diodes and transistors are non-linear.
Series resistances add: R_total = R1 + R2.

ohms-law-calculator.quickAnswer: Ohm's Law: V = I x R, and power P = V x I. With 12 V across 4 ohms, current is 12 / 4 = 3 A and power is 12 x 3 = 36 W. Enter any two of voltage, current, resistance, or power above and the calculator finds the rest.

ohms-law-calculator.workedExample:
Known: V = 12 V, R = 4 ohms.
1. Current: I = V / R = 12 / 4 = 3 A.
2. Power: P = V x I = 12 x 3 = 36 W. (Check: P = V^2 / R = 144 / 4 = 36 W.)
3. Resistance stays 4 ohms.

Another: P = 60 W, V = 120 V -> I = 60 / 120 = 0.5 A, R = 120^2 / 60 = 240 ohms.
